idiom_name: Channel.receive/tryReceive + delay backoff in a coroutine
implementation_notes: Coroutines replace the poll loop with suspending calls: channel.receive() suspends until an element is available, tryReceive()/receiveCatching() provide the immediate receiveNoWait-style variants, and delay() is the cancellable idle backoff, so the consumer's structured scope - not a receive timeout - becomes the shutdown path. The explicit timed pull is still the right shape for poll-based clients such as KafkaConsumer.poll(Duration), where the batch bound and idle policy remain application decisions.
pitfalls: delay() is what keeps the loop cooperative; Thread.sleep() inside a coroutine blocks the dispatcher thread and makes cancellation unobservable.
receive() throws once the channel is closed, so a loop without receiveCatching()/tryReceive() dies at the first close instead of draining what is left and exiting cleanly.
